engagement.note: Lilly's STZ-diabetic rat gave peglispro a prolonged duration of glucose lowering vs lispro; opening entry, no human comparison drawn yet.
engagement.short: STZ rat: peglispro prolonged glucose lowering
engagement.quote: BIL exhibited a markedly longer time to maximum concentration after subcutaneous injection, a greater area under the concentration-time curve, and a longer duration of action in the STZ-treated diabetic rat than insulin lispro.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. 2016 is the publication date (epub 2016-03-29); the rat studies were run before the IMAGINE phase 3 programme (2011) but no earlier citable source was found, so 2016 is a proxy for first use.

engagement.note: Healthy-subject euglycaemic clamps: peglispro glucose infusion rate sustained ≥36 h while glargine waned at 24 h, the prolonged action the STZ rat showed.
engagement.short: Human clamp: peglispro GIR sustained ≥36 h
engagement.quote: LY2605541 glucose infusion rate (GIR) profiles were sustained for ≥36 hours versus glargine GIR profiles, which waned at 24 hours.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides. The human clamp (epub 2014-02-13) predates the rat paper (2016-03-29); the entry is dated 2016, when the pairing first became possible. Healthy volunteers, not T2D patients.
engagement.judgement: Same, direction only: the rat's readout (duration of glucose lowering after one SC dose, longer than the short-acting comparator) moved the same way in dosed humans (GIR sustained >=36 h vs glargine 24 h). Pairing is the drafter's; the rat exposures are not matched to human ones in either abstract. This is the same Lilly STZ-rat system later used for efsitora (Moyers 2022), so peglispro opens the track.
engagement.magnitude_basis: duration of glucose-lowering action after a single subcutaneous dose vs comparator insulin

engagement.note: Efsitora in T2D patients and healthy subjects: t1/2 ~17 days and a sustained dose-dependent fall in fasting glucose for >=5 days after one dose, as the STZ rat (>=1 week) had shown.
engagement.short: Efsitora: week-long glucose lowering held in T2D
engagement.quote: BIF had a PK half-life of approximately 17 days, which led to a sustained, dose-dependent decrease in fasting blood glucose for 5 days or longer.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; sponsor-authored phase 1 (single ascending dose in healthy participants and T2D; multiple dose in T2D). Pairing with the STZ rat is the drafter's.
engagement.reason: Rat's week-long glucose lowering held in humans
engagement.judgement: Second member on the track, entered as strengthens: the STZ rat predicted glucose lowering to normoglycaemia for at least a week after one SC dose of efsitora (Moyers 2022; FDA 761408 integrated review lines 1125-1127), and single doses in humans lowered fasting glucose for 5 days or longer with a flat weekly profile (peak-to-trough 1.14 at steady state). Direction only on the PD readout; the rat under-predicted the PK half-life (~120 h vs ~17 days), which is scored on the dose cell.
engagement.magnitude_basis: duration of fasting-glucose lowering after a single subcutaneous dose

dose.note: The STZ rat set peglispro's protraction target (longer duration of action than lispro, once-daily basal); human PK not yet paired.
dose.short: STZ rat sets peglispro protraction target
dose.quote: BIL exhibited a markedly longer time to maximum concentration after subcutaneous injection, a greater area under the concentration-time curve, and a longer duration of action in the STZ-treated diabetic rat than insulin lispro.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; 2016 is a proxy for first use (publication date of studies run before the 2011 phase 3 start).

dose.note: Peglispro's once-daily basal regimen was reached in humans (t1/2 24-45 h, flat profile, tolerated) and worked in IMAGINE 2; the rat's protraction target was met.
dose.quote: These results established a well-tolerated baseline dose for LY2605541 with a relatively flat PK profile and low intra-subject variability.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Human PK paper epub 2014-02-13; dated 2016 when the rat side was published. 'Worked' is IMAGINE 2 (Davies 2016, doi:10.1111/dom.12712, HbA1c non-inferior and superior to glargine). No rat half-life is given in the abstract, so no scaling magnitude.
dose.judgement: Same by the table's 'reached, drug worked' row: the regimen the rat's prolonged action was built to deliver (once-daily basal) was reached at a tolerated dose and the HbA1c primary was met. The rat stated no tolerability margin, so margin_stated is null. Peglispro was later stopped on liver safety, which is scored on the chronic toxicology track, not as a dose failure.
dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval supported by the duration of action (once daily)

dose.note: Efsitora's once-weekly regimen, read off the rat's >=1-week normoglycaemia, was reached and tolerated in humans; the rat t1/2 (~120 h) under-predicted the human ~17 days by ~3x.
dose.short: Weekly efsitora regimen reached; rat t1/2 ~3x short
dose.quote: BIF was well tolerated and the PK/PD profile enabled once-weekly dosing with minimal variation in exposure in a treatment interval of 1 week.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level, sponsor-authored. Rat half-life ~120 h from the Moyers 2022 abstract (FDA 761408 integrated review gives 82-147 h); human ~17 days (~408 h), ratio ~3.4x. 'Worked' is the phase 2 (Bue-Valleskey 2023, NCT04450394) and QWINT-2 (NCT05362058).
dose.reason: Weekly target reached; rat t1/2 scaled short
dose.judgement: Strengthens the 2016 same with a second member: the rat said one dose holds normoglycaemia for at least a week, the once-weekly regimen was reached at tolerated doses and met its HbA1c primary in T2D, so the dose target was met; the rat under-predicted the human half-life about 3.4-fold, recorded as off_by_2-5x, the same direction as the Novo track's rat/dog/pig scaling for icodec. No tolerability margin was stated by the rat; hypoglycaemia in normoglycaemic toxicology animals is exaggerated pharmacology and is not a dose finding here.
dose.magnitude_basis: terminal half-life: STZ rat ~120 h vs human ~17 days (~408 h)

efficacy.note: The STZ rat showed prolonged glucose lowering for peglispro; no patient HbA1c result paired yet.
efficacy.quote: BIL exhibited a markedly longer time to maximum concentration after subcutaneous injection, a greater area under the concentration-time curve, and a longer duration of action in the STZ-treated diabetic rat than insulin lispro.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; 2016 is a proxy for first use (publication date of studies run before the 2011 phase 3 start).

efficacy.note: IMAGINE 2: peglispro non-inferior (and superior) to glargine on HbA1c at 52 weeks in insulin-naive T2D, the glucose lowering the STZ rat predicted.
efficacy.quote: Peglispro was non-inferior to glargine in HbA1c reduction [least-squares (LS) mean difference: -0.29%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.40, -0.19]
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; pairing with the rat is the drafter's. Registry results for NCT01435616 were posted 2018-04-13, after the paper (epub 2016-08-12).
efficacy.judgement: Same, not neg: the rat's own data for peglispro were not below the class bar (prolonged glucose lowering, full agonism) and the HbA1c primary was met. The programme was stopped on liver fat and ALT, a harm the single-dose rat study was not designed to show and that is scored once, on the rat/dog chronic toxicology track. Direction only: a treat-to-target trial does not test the magnitude a rat glucose curve predicts. The pharmacology predicts a surrogate; no outcome trial was run for peglispro.

patient_trials.quote: Peglispro was non-inferior to glargine in HbA1c reduction [least-squares (LS) mean difference: -0.29%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.40, -0.19]

efficacy.note: Efsitora phase 2 in insulin-naive T2D: HbA1c non-inferior to degludec at 26 weeks (results posted 2022-11-02); QWINT-2 confirmed at 52 weeks in 2024.
efficacy.quote: After 26 weeks of treatment, BIF demonstrated a noninferior HbA1c change from baseline versus degludec, with a treatment difference of 0.06% (90% CI -0.11, 0.24; P = 0.56).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Dated 2022 by the registry results posting for NCT04450394 (2022-11-02), which preceded the paper (Diabetes Care, 2023); the rat side (Moyers 2022, epub 2022-07-15) was public by then. Pairing is the drafter's.
efficacy.reason: Both Lilly members met their HbA1c primary
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens with the second member: the rat predicted week-long glucose lowering for efsitora and the phase 2 and phase 3 (QWINT-2) HbA1c primaries in T2D were met against degludec. Direction only. The T1D trial (QWINT-5) also met its HbA1c primary but is another disease and is not scored here. No outcome trial has been run; outcome_tested stays null.

patient_trials.quote: After 26 weeks of treatment, BIF demonstrated a noninferior HbA1c change from baseline versus degludec, with a treatment difference of 0.06% (90% CI -0.11, 0.24; P = 0.56).
(estimated treatment difference, -0.09 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.22 to 0.04), findings that showed noninferiority.

safety.note: Single-dose PK/PD in insulin-deficient rats; the study stated no harm prediction and reported none. Mitogenicity was read in cells (its own track).
safety.short: Single-dose STZ rat: no harm stated
safety.quote: Streptozotocin (STZ)-treated diabetic rats were used to study the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics of BIL.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; 2016 is a proxy for first use. Peglispro's liver harm is scored once, on the rat/dog chronic toxicology track, not here.

safety.note: QWINT-5 (T1D, imported): severe hypoglycaemia 10% on efsitora vs 3% on degludec; the insulin-deficient rat, dosed once to normoglycaemia for a week, was silent on it.
safety.short: T1D severe hypoglycaemia missed by STZ rat
safety.quote: Severe hypoglycaemia incidence was higher with efsitora (35 [10%] of 343) versus degludec (11 [3%] of 349) during weeks 0-52.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Imported from T1D (MONDO:0005147): in this context's own T2D programme severe hypoglycaemia was uncommon and balanced (12 vs 14 subjects) and level 2/3 rate ratios were 1.1-1.3, none significant (FDA 761408 integrated review). The rat was never run against a titrated daily comparator, so this is silence contradicted, not a wrong prediction. Registry results for NCT05463744 posted 2025-06-24.
safety.reason: Rat silent; T1D severe hypoglycaemia excess
safety.judgement: Contra on a missed on-target harm the species could show: hypoglycaemia is measurable in rats (the normoglycaemic toxicology animals showed it, with mortality) and the STZ rat, the nearest animal to exogenous-insulin-dependent T1D, reported only normoglycaemia for at least a week after one dose (Moyers 2022; FDA 761408 integrated review lines 1125-1127). In T1D patients efsitora gave a higher rate of level 2/3 hypoglycaemia (rate ratio 1.21) and three times the severe-hypoglycaemia incidence of degludec, which the FDA attributed to 'a long-acting, slowly adjustable basal insulin in a population entirely dependent on exogenous insulin' and which became a label limitation of use. Transferred under the safety rule for comparisons made in another population, flagged imported_from; low confidence because the context's own T2D trials did not show it and a single-dose rat study cannot model dose titration. Counted once here; the same harm is not entered on the chronic toxicology track. The efsitora malignancy imbalance (1.4% vs 1.0%) belongs to the in-vitro mitogenicity track, not this one.

considered_not_added: Degludec three-times-weekly regimen failure (FDA 2015 SumR lines 705-712; Zinman 2013, doi:10.1016/S2213-8587(13)70013-5): a regimen read off the pig clamp / rat-dog PK protraction, so a dose entry on the existing novo-pig-clamp-rat-dog-pk track, not a new system; left to that track.

Icodec's selection model, the dog intravenous half-life screen with rat SC potency (Kjeldsen 2021, doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.1c00257) and the diabetic-rat / normoglycaemic dog and pig glucose lowering in FDA 761326 PharmR lines 88-96: dog and rat PK are already the 'rat/dog PK' half of the existing novo-pig-clamp-rat-dog-pk track, whose 2026 dose entry quotes the same rat/dog/pig half-lives, and the draft's 2021 engagement entry already names the icodec diabetic-rat data as its model_src; same system, so at most a model_src refinement on that track.

Icodec hypoglycaemia (FDA 761326 SumR 2026 lines 184-186, 442-443; T1D CRL 2024-07-10, ONWARDS 6) against the pig clamp's 'close to even distribution' claim: a safety entry on the existing Novo track, not a new system.
Degludec's stated lower-hypoglycaemia prediction (FDA 2015 SumR lines 707-709) met by BEGIN Once Long and DEVOTE: a safety same on the existing Novo pig-clamp track, not a new system.

Efsitora malignancy imbalance (FDA 761408 IntegratedR lines 714-715, 812-821; 1.4% vs 1.0%, judged not causal) against Lilly's SAOS-2/H4IIE proliferation and IGF-1R assays (Moyers 2022): the same in-vitro mitogenicity system as the existing insulin-mitogenicity-cells track, so it belongs there; the efsitora QWINT-5 hypoglycaemia lead was taken onto the new STZ-rat track instead (safety 2024, imported).

EX1000 (Novo Nordisk investigational insulin formulation; phase 2 T2D trials NCT00698802 and NCT00660374, 2008-09, no results posted): not a model system and no preclinical model or patient result found; a context-note correction for the draft, scores nothing.

Lilly rat euglycaemic clamp with EGP/FFA/muscle glucose uptake (FDA 761408 IntegratedR, study DBT215: glucose control at ~2000-fold higher concentrations than lispro, +10% FFA, -33% muscle uptake) and mouse liver/muscle Akt phosphorylation (DBT214): hepato-preferential readouts in normoglycaemic animals; no human tracer clamp with hepatic balance for efsitora was found to pair them with, and the peglispro equivalent is the existing lilly-dog-hepatic-clamp track; no patient comparison found.

Model-based PK/PD simulations used to choose the efsitora loading dose (1.5-3x weekly dose; Heise 2023, Frias 2023) and icodec's loading-dose and titration algorithms: built from human phase 1 PK, not preclinical models (same reasoning as the FLT3 tile's exclusion of population PK models); not added.

Patient-derived cells, organoids or ex-vivo sensitivity for degludec, icodec, efsitora or peglispro: Europe PMC search returned 76 hits, none comparing a patient's ex-vivo result with that patient's response to a member drug; no patient-level system exists for this class.
Human genetic models (INSR loss-of-function syndromes) and human challenge models: no comparison with a member drug's patient result found; not added.
